text:
The laws by which you judge, Batinus, you study less than sell; you understand what is bought; the Fleece pleases you more than Jason.


Interpreting human and divine law, you offend them, and as you shrink or stretch it, your hand prepares the verdict.


You cannot hear cheap pleas; only payment dispels doubts; bargains govern you, not texts.


Since intent and interest do not change, wash hands with Pilate or hang with Judas by your purse.

translation.title: To a Judge Who Is Merchandise
